messages:
ana (support): customer (acme-inc) reporting transient 403s on decrypt after key rotation. They say decrypts used to succeed, started failing ~08:34 UTC. Customer on Private deployment, customer-managed KMS + HSM proxy in their VPC. attaching our error snippet.

ashley (sec): thanks — can you paste the exact error and any CloudTrail entries you have? my first suspects: encryption-context mismatch or key policy condition (kms:ViaService / kms:EncryptionContext) preventing decrypt via our assumed role.

samir (oncall): also need to know whether the KMS key is cross-account and if our agent is using an assumed role or a grants path. grants can take a few seconds to propagate after rotation/alias swap.

ana (support): typo, meant ana — pasted logs below from our runtime around the time of the 403s:

```
2026-03-16T21:34:12Z ERROR decrypt failed status=403 err=\"AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 (Service: AWSKMS; Status Code: 403; Error Code: AccessDeniedException)\"
request_id=aa11bb22cc33
customer_key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
caller_role=arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-agent-role
```

ashley (sec): OK. can you check CloudTrail for that request id and paste RequestParameters.encryptionContext if present? If absent, that points to the caller not forwarding the context. Many key policies restrict decrypt to requests with a matching encryption context.

bryan (infra): I pulled the CloudTrail event for aa11bb22cc33. interestingly, our decrypt call shows encryptionContext: {} (empty) while the original encrypt event stored client:acme. The key policy contains a Condition: ForAllValues:StringEquals on kms:EncryptionContext with key \"client\" -> \"acme\". decrypt was denied due to missing context.

repro steps I ran locally: 
1) success case (explicit context):
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 --encryption-context client=acme --profile acme
# -> returns plaintext
```
2) failure case (no context):
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 --profile acme
# -> AccessDeniedException
```

bryan (infra): digging deeper: customer has an HSM proxy (their side) that issues a signed token which our agent uses to call KMS. The proxy reserializes the request and currently doesn't propagate the encryption-context metadata into the signed request it issues. CloudTrail shows our decrypt request arrives with SigV4 but without encryption context headers.

samir (oncall): that explains it. short-term mitigation: we should detect missing encryptionContext in our middleware and return a structured error pointing customers to the exact policy mismatch (helps customer ops). longer term: the HSM proxy must preserve encryption context when it signs/forwards requests. Also check for any kms:ViaService conditions in the key policy that could block cross-account calls via a proxy service.

ana (support): customer is blocked — their app caches decrypted tokens, so a lot of downstream API calls are failing (500/401). they asked for ETA on a patch.

ashley (sec): action plan: 
- @bryan: hotfix the HSM proxy to pass through encryptionContext and add an e2e test that decrypt with/without context reproduces policy behavior. aim: ship to staging tonight.
- @samir: add a runtime check to log and return a clear error when encryptionContext is missing (include key arn and request_id), and attach CloudTrail link for audit.
- @ana: update the customer that we found a likely cause (encryption-context stripped) and we'll patch tonight; escalate to enterprise ops for any compliance tracking. :thumbsup:

kms-bot: created ticket INFRA-7892, PR #4523 opened, staging deploy queued.

bryan (infra): opening PR now. note to reviewers: include unit test that asserts header \"x-amz-encryption-context\" (and serialized context in signed token) survives proxy signing. I'll also add log correlation id so CloudTrail -> our logs mapping is straightforward.

ana (support): told customer we expect a patch in <=24h, added workaround: they can add a temporary key policy exception (not ideal) or re-encrypt objects removing encryption-context. customer chose wait for our patch.

ashley (sec): also filing a compliance note: audit logs show decrypt attempts and AccessDenied; capture these events for retention per our data-retention policy. I'll attach CloudTrail snapshots to the incident ticket.

samir (oncall): after patch, let's run a canary with the customer's staging workload and verify CloudTrail shows the encryptionContext present in decrypt events.

ana (support): thanks team, I'll keep the customer updated.
